items.followUp: Which tag is used to define the body section of an HTML document?

rubric.description: Names the correct HTML tag for the head section.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the head tag.

rubric.why: Shows how the tag is used in an HTML document.
rubric.description: States that the head section contains document information or metadata.
rubric.how: Award for a correct explanation of the tag’s role.

modelAnswer: The head section of an HTML document is enclosed in the <head> and </head> tags.
It contains information about the document, such as its title.

rubric.why: States what happens to stored information when power is removed.
rubric.description: Says that non-volatile memory retains its data.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the data is retained.

rubric.why: Identifies the condition under which the data is retained.
rubric.description: States that data remains stored when power is off or removed.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning that the memory retains data without power.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is switched off.
Examples include ROM and flash memory.

items.followUp: Convert (173)₁₀ into the binary number system.

rubric.why: Shows a valid method for converting the decimal number to binary.
rubric.description: Demonstrates repeated division by 2 or a correct sum of powers of 2.
rubric.how: Award for a valid conversion method.

rubric.description: Gives the correct binary representation of 156.

modelAnswer: Given: (156)₁₀
156 ÷ 2 = 78, remainder 0
78 ÷ 2 = 39, remainder 0
39 ÷ 2 = 19, remainder 1
19 ÷ 2 = 9, remainder 1
9 ÷ 2 = 4, remainder 1
4 ÷ 2 = 2, remainder 0
2 ÷ 2 = 1, remainder 0
1 ÷ 2 = 0, remainder 1
Read the remainders from bottom to top: (156)₁₀ = (10011100)₂

items.followUp: What is meant by the OR operator?

rubric.why: States the condition for an AND operation to produce true.
rubric.description: Says that AND gives true when both inputs are true.
rubric.how: Award for the correct true condition.

rubric.why: Shows the result when the true condition is not met.
rubric.description: States that the result is false if either input is false.
rubric.how: Award for the correct false condition.

modelAnswer: The AND operator is a logical operator that gives a true result only when both inputs are true.
If either input is false, the result is false.

rubric.why: Identifies the unauthorized copying of software as the central idea.
rubric.description: Defines softlifting as unauthorized or illegal copying of software.
rubric.how: Award for identifying unauthorized software copying.

rubric.why: Distinguishes softlifting by giving its common form.
rubric.description: Mentions installing or using one licensed copy on multiple computers without permission.
rubric.how: Award for the multiple-computer example or equivalent explanation.

modelAnswer: Softlifting is the unauthorized copying or installation of software.
A common example is installing one licensed copy of a program on several computers without permission.

items.followUp: What is video conferencing? Give an example.

rubric.why: Defines application sharing as joint access to or use of an application.
rubric.description: Explains that users can share or use an application over a network.
rubric.how: Award for a correct definition of application sharing.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer includes a relevant example.
rubric.description: Gives an example, such as users collaborating on a document in Google Docs.
rubric.how: Award for a valid application-sharing example.

modelAnswer: Application sharing allows people in different locations to access or use the same application over a network.
For example, several users can work on the same document using Google Docs.

items.followUp: What is the function of the IP part of TCP/IP?

rubric.why: Identifies TCP/IP as a set of communication rules or protocols.
rubric.description: Defines TCP/IP as a protocol suite used for communication between computers.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as the Internet communication protocol suite.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of the two protocol names represented by TCP/IP.
rubric.description: Names TCP as Transmission Control Protocol and IP as Internet Protocol, or explains their roles.
rubric.how: Award for correctly naming the components or describing their communication roles.

modelAnswer: TCP/IP is a suite of communication protocols used to connect computers and exchange data over the Internet.
TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol, and IP stands for Internet Protocol.

items.followUp: What is the function of a switch in a computer network?

rubric.why: States that a router connects networks.
rubric.description: Explains that a router connects two or more networks.
rubric.how: Award for identifying its network-connecting function.

rubric.why: Describes how the router directs data between networks.
rubric.description: States that it forwards or routes data packets, typically using IP addresses.
rubric.how: Award for explaining packet forwarding or routing.

modelAnswer: A router is a networking device that connects two or more networks.
It forwards data packets between networks, using IP addresses to direct them to their destinations.
